StatDef.label: embodied labor: extraction
StatDef.description: Labor spent at the point of extraction — mining, harvesting, and butchery — to obtain the raw materials embodied in this thing, per unit.\n\nMeasured in seconds of colonist work at nominal work speed, following the cheapest chain of production that could yield this thing. Nature contributes nothing: an ore vein's labor content is the work of mining it, not what the ore is worth.

StatDef.label: embodied labor: fabrication
StatDef.description:
Labor spent transforming materials into this thing — crafting, smithing, cooking, construction — summed over every production step, per unit.

Measured in seconds of colonist work at nominal work speed. Excludes the extraction labor embodied in the inputs, which is reported separately.

RimWorld's own pricing pays roughly fourteen times more for a second of extraction labor than for a second of fabrication labor, so a thing dominated by this stat is one whose labor the economy barely rewards.
